The page names Luhak Agam, Tanah Datar, Luhak Limo Puluah, Rao and Pasaman and gives no map, so the shape is the Minangkabau highlands minus the Padang-Pariaman coast (the pagaruyung-kingdom dossier's own 1609 reading). ledger.note: 1803: the Padri movement begins. The war 'was fought from 1803 until 1837' in West Sumatra; the early conflict began in 1803, 'before Dutch intervention, when the Padri began suppressing customs they saw as un-Islamic'. The page names the leaders (Tuanku Nan Renceh, Tuanku Imam Bonjol) and Luhak Agam, Tanah Datar, Luhak Limo Puluah, Rao and Pasaman; the highlands are the reading.

1815: the Padri attack Pagaruyung. 'In 1815, the Padri under the leadership of Tuanku Lintau attacked the Pagaruyung Kingdom'; Raffles in 1818 'only found the remains of Pagaruyung Royal Palace which was burned down'. The page does not say 'occupied'; the pagaruyung-kingdom dossier records an occupation from 1815.

region.text: Simawang and Sulit Air, near Lake Singkarak (placed by the researcher)

ledger.note: April 1821: the Dutch join the war. 'On 21 February 1821 ... the Minangkabau nobility made a deal with the Dutch in Padang to help them fight the Padri'; 'In April 1821, Dutch troops attacked Simawang and Sulit Air.'

March 1822: the Padri leave Pagaruyung. The page is silent on when the Padri left Tanah Datar; the date (4 March 1822) is the pagaruyung-kingdom dossier's, from a page not opened here. [Reviewer se-03-x, 2026-10-24: confidence raised from 1: the Padri War page has 'On 4 March 1822' Dutch troops under Raaff 'succeeded in pushing the Padri people out of Pagaruyung']

ledger.note: 1824: the Treaty of Masang. The skirmishes of 1821-1824 ended 'only by the Treaty of Masang'; the war then cooled for about six years because of the Java War.

wars.outcome: Dutch victory: after a civil war within the Minangkabau, the Dutch allied with the adat nobility (21 February 1821), fought the Padri 1821-1824 (Treaty of Masang), again from 1831 (Lintau, Luhak Limo Puluah 1832, the Long Plakat of 1833) and took Fort Bonjol on 16 August 1837.
wars.note: The page does not mention Imam Bonjol's capture or exile in October 1837, nor resistance at Dalu-Dalu in 1838.

certainty.note: No map and no boundaries on the page; the highlands are intermixed adat, Padri and Dutch lands, with the Dutch holding the coast.

notes: Written 2026-10-24 by the se-03-x additions batch, as the counterpart 'padri-movement' named by the dutch-east-indies and pagaruyung-kingdom ledgers. One page opened (Padri War). Unsettled: (1) the page gives no territory list beyond the names Luhak Agam, Tanah Datar, Luhak Limo Puluah, Rao and Pasaman, no map and no dates for the Padri's spread; the shape is the whole highlands region (the one the pagaruyung dossier uses) minus the west coast, which is too large for the early years; (2) the Pagaruyung occupation of 1815 is 'attacked' on this page, 'occupied' in the sibling dossier, and the sibling's 4 March 1822 is not on this page (confidence 1); (3) Imam Bonjol's capture, the Dalu-Dalu resistance of 1838, the Plakat Panjang's effect on borders and the Second Padri War's first year (1831) are only partly on the page; Pagaruyung's own dossier ends in 1833 with the sultan's arrest; (4) Bonjol's coordinates are approximate and the discs for Limo Puluah and Lintau are placed by the researcher; (5) type rebel for a reformist movement that governed land and fought the adat nobility as well as the Dutch. Gazetteer: Luhak Agam, Tanah Datar, Luhak Limo Puluah, Payakumbuh, Lintau, Bonjol, Pasaman, Rao.
